newsitem.title: UK: Gibraltar to ask for new relationship with Britain.
newsitem.headline: Gibraltar to ask for new relationship with Britain.

text.p: The Chief Minister of Gibraltar called on Sunday for the tiny enclave bordering southern Spain to be granted a new relationship with Britain as a Crown Dependency.

Peter Caruana said he would put the idea to Foreign Secretary Robin Cook at a meeting on Monday, telling him the "Rock's" 30,000 people wanted to "shed the stigma of being a colony because (of) all the imagery that that conjures up".
He told Sky television in an interview the proposed change would put Gibraltar, whose sovereignty is contested by Madrid, on the same footing as the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man.
They are internally self-governing territories for whose foreign relations Britain takes responsibility.

"The Channel Islands and Isle of Man are simply examples of how it is possible to have a close political constitutional relationship with the United Kingdom without being part of the UK and without it being a colonial relationship," he said.
"That is what we aim for -- to be a Crown Dependency as opposed to a dependent territory."
Caruana's meeting with Cook comes less than a week after Britain handed sovereignty its largest remaining colony, Hong Kong, back to China.
He said he saw no parallels between Gibraltar and Hong Kong as Gibraltar had a well-established democracy and Britain held it permanently rather than on a limited lease.
